videos.title: Anatomy of Good Icons
videos.why: Layout, stroke thickness (0:57) and corner treatment (1:53) in under four minutes; these are exactly the things lab-icons asks you to spot when one icon breaks the set.

videos.title: Decorative Images: Delightful or Dreadful?
videos.why: Decorative images can set tone, but they must never get in the way of the task; ask that of every hero image an AI tool adds to your pages.

podcasts.episode: Susan Kare: Designing Icons & Graphics For the Original Mac
podcasts.why: The designer of many of the original Macintosh icons on how small symbols made a new kind of computer feel understandable; listen for how she thinks about making a picture readable in very few pixels.

podcasts.episode: 42. Icons that Work (feat Kate Kaplan, Insights Architect @ NN/g)
podcasts.why: Kate Kaplan on what her research for the book Digital Icons That Work found about which icons people understand; the companion to the NN/g icon video and article.

reads.title: Icon Usability
reads.why: Only a few icons, such as home, print and the magnifying glass for search, are close to universal, so most icons need a text label; check every unlabelled icon in your app against it.

reads.title: Designing icons
reads.why: The grid behind this lesson's icon figure, with a 24dp icon, a 20dp live area, 2dp of padding and keyline shapes that keep round, square and wide icons visually balanced.

reads.title: Photos as Web Content
reads.why: Eyetracking shows people ignore generic feel-good pictures and study images that carry information, such as product shots and photos of real people; a test for every image you add.
